beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Thirty days ago, I gave Claude Code one job: run a YouTube channel for me. No face, no voice, no editing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It wrote the scripts, drew the animation, voiced every line and uploaded three Shorts a day, while I slept.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: After a month it had made {fact1} videos, earned {fact3} views and {fact4} subscribers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Is that a win or a flop? Stay to the end, because the most useful part is everything that went wrong.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: I'll show you the setup, the first week, the hit, the crash, the robots that fix themselves, and the final scoreboard.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter one. The setup.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day one. I opened Claude Code and described the channel I wanted: animated money stories, true facts only, and every number checked by code.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And I didn't write the code myself. I described what I wanted, and Claude Code wrote it: the renderer, the uploader, the checks, tens of thousands of lines.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It built a whole studio. A planner picks the topic, a writer storyboards it, code checks the maths, and a second AI checks every fact.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then it draws the animation and an offline voice reads it. No stock footage, no downloaded music. Every frame and every sound is made in code.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It even invented a cast: Rohan, Priya, Sharma, and a coin called Sikka.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Finished videos go up to GitHub, and a scheduler uploads them at three fixed times a day. It all runs in the cloud, on free tiers and one Claude subscription.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It also built me a dashboard, so I can see every video, every upload and every robot's work from my phone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So I pressed go and went to sleep. Would anyone actually watch?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter two. Week one.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Day one was a prototype. Day two, the first Short went live. By the end of the week, it was making videos every single day.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The first Shorts were about savings, budgets and credit cards. And almost nobody watched them, a few dozen views each.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Budget tips are what every channel already makes. Mine were just one more drop in the ocean.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then one topic broke through. Billionaires.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And that one topic changed the whole plan.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter three. The hit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The best Short asked why billionaires can't just pay a small tax. It reached {fact6} views.

params.title: Why can't billionaires just pay a tax?
params.label: Views

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And it wasn't alone. Why billionaires never sell their stock, what a billion looks like in hundred dollar bills: every Short past a thousand views was about huge sums of money.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The numbers were clear. Big money titles had a median of {fact15} views. Personal budget titles, just {fact16}.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The audience surprised me too. Stories about one country stayed small. Stories about famous people and companies travelled all over the world.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Its best day brought in {fact13} views. So the system rewrote its own rules: big money first, global stories, and Shorts under thirty five seconds.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It felt like the channel had found its thing. Then the views fell off a cliff.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter four. The crash.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In early November, views dropped by about nine in ten. The median Short got just {fact7} views.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: YouTube Studio told me why. On the worst Short, {fact14} of the people it was shown to swiped away, most of them in the very first second.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And things broke. {fact11} videos failed the checks and were thrown away. One night GitHub skipped the uploads for nine hours, and a slot went empty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Long videos were even harder. One of them was shown to a hundred people, and only four clicked.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That's the thing about an automated channel. It doesn't fail loudly. It fails quietly, at three in the morning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So I gave it something most channels don't have: a team of robots that fixes itself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter five. The agents.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Every night, eight AI agents wake up. An auditor checks every number against YouTube. A researcher finds what people are watching this week.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: An improver tests one change at a time on half the Shorts, and keeps it only if viewers stay longer. A reviewer watches our own videos frame by frame and writes down every mistake.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And no agent can change anything on its own. A guard checks every edit first, and runs the tests.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: In thirty days the agents tried {fact8} changes to their own system. The guard let {fact9} through and blocked {fact10}.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So after thirty days, here's the honest scoreboard.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Chapter six. Scoreboard.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Altogether, my faceless channel got {fact3} views.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The system made {fact1} videos and published {fact2}. They were watched for {fact5} hours and brought in {fact4} subscribers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: So, a win or a flop? Honestly, both. As a channel, it is still tiny. As a machine that makes, checks and improves its own videos every single day, it is the most interesting thing I have ever built.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Lesson one: automation makes videos. It does not make people care.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Lesson two: the topic is the whole game. Big money beat budget tips every single time.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Lesson three: the first second decides everything. {fact12} of my views came from the Shorts feed, where people swipe in a heartbeat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And lesson four: measure, don't guess. Every rule this channel follows today came from its own numbers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Next, it learns from videos I pick myself, and tests one change a week. I'll show you how that goes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And if you want to try this yourself, start with the topic, not the tools. The tools are the easy part now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Would you let AI run your channel? Tell me in the comments.
